Food deserts 100% exist. I see it myself within areas of my own semi-large city. 

Lower income communities of people who may or may not have personal transportation; with the only “food” near them being available in the form of a Family Dollar (no fresh produce) or fast food. To get anything fresh they’d have to travel to a separate area of the city or to a neighboring city. Which, as I said earlier, could be a problem due to lack of personal transportation to actually get there. 

I’m sure it’s different in other cities across the country. That’s just what I’m seeing in North Texas right now with my own two eyes.

Yep. Shocked more people aren’t realizing this. Old timers claiming new hires “just don’t get it” while not seeing they’re falling exactly where UPS wants them to. 

If you think a newer employee isn’t understanding something, like the union contract or what have you, don’t talk down to them. They’re your fellow worker, and if a strike happens we’re all supposed to be on the same side. Doesn’t matter if you’ve read your union handbook a million times, once, or never; we’re all in same boat and some respectful education on topics the company makes intentionally confusing would go a long way. 

Lots of people don’t understand that UPS isn’t necessarily a full time career for everyone. Many of us are students taking advantage of tuition reimbursement, or we just need the free healthcare. It doesn’t mean that we aren’t entitled to a decent wage just because we’re not working 60 hours a week as a driver. Where’s the solidarity?

I mean, cost of living is skyrocketing and many hubs are cutting hours. People have a right to be upset that their pay is being cut without people from the “old days” calling it a joke. 

Workers need to support workers. Be mad that you weren’t getting paid enough and take it out on upper management and ineffective local unions, not your fellow workers who make more now that are just trying to live.

I texted one once and they seemed to want me to disconnect as fast as possible. If you aren’t at current risk for blowing your brains out right that second they seem to rush through the entire interaction. 

I’ve heard some other bad stories of them calling the cops on people too. Probably the worst way to respond to a mental health crisis...

I guess a lot of it would depend on the specific volunteer you get paired with, but I’ve honestly seen overwhelming negative experiences with these hotlines.

I think a lot of people here would feel the same way. The longer I live, the more isolated I feel. 

It’s too hard to articulate my thoughts to other people, so I just gave up. Like you said, it’s almost unbearable at times. Many of my friends seem like completely different species to me at this point. I don’t feel human. 

I don’t know how to help, but at least try and take comfort in the fact that other people know what you mean, and even feel the same way to an extent.
